title: He Won $1 Million, Then He Was Arrested Days Later
summary:
Ariel Antonio Velasquez-Morales won $1 million on a scratch ticket in Massachusetts. In a photo from the Massachusetts State Lottery, he held a big check and smiled. It was the first puzzle ticket he had ever scratched. He matched 11 words on a $10 ticket, and local news said he planned to save and invest the money.

Days later, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, known as ICE, said it had arrested him. ICE said officers arrested him on Tuesday, November 24, in East Boston, Massachusetts. The agency said he will stay in ICE custody until he is removed from the United States. ICE said he entered the country illegally on May 15, 2013, and an immigration judge ordered him removed on April 24, 2014.

ICE said the lottery ticket “ultimately led to his arrest,” but did not explain how. He does not yet appear on ICE's Online Detainee Locator System. It is unclear if he has a lawyer. A woman who said she is his sister-in-law asked on Facebook for respect and empathy for him, his wife and children.
why_it_matters: This story shows how one big moment, like winning a prize, can be followed by a very different one, and why it matters to understand the rules that affect people and families in a community.

background_read: A scratch ticket is a lottery card where you scratch off a coating to see if you have won a prize.
In the United States, a government agency called ICE is in charge of enforcing immigration rules, and it can hold people who do not have permission to live in the country.
A judge can order a person to leave the country, and that order can be carried out later if the person is found by the agency.
